files.src/textkit/slug.py:
"""URL slug generation."""

from __future__ import annotations


def slugify(text: str, sep: str = "-") -> str:
    """Convert ``text`` into a lowercase URL slug.

    Runs of non-alphanumeric characters collapse into a single separator, and
    leading/trailing separators are stripped.

    Args:
        text: Input text.
        sep: Separator character to use between words.

    Returns:
        The slugified string.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sep`` is not exactly one character.
    """
    if len(sep) != 1:
        raise ValueError("sep must be a single character")

    pieces: list[str] = []
    previous_was_separator = False
    for char in text.lower():
        if char.isalnum():
            pieces.append(char)
            previous_was_separator = False
        elif not previous_was_separator:
            pieces.append(sep)
            previous_was_separator = True
    return "".join(pieces).strip(sep)

files.src/textkit/wrap.py:
"""Greedy word wrapping."""

from __future__ import annotations


def wrap_text(text: str, width: int) -> list[str]:
    """Wrap ``text`` into lines of at most ``width`` characters.

    Args:
        text: Input text. Runs of whitespace separate words.
        width: Maximum line length. Must be at least 1.

    Returns:
        The wrapped lines, without trailing whitespace. Empty input yields an
        empty list.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``width`` is less than 1.
    """
    if width < 1:
        raise ValueError("width must be at least 1")

    lines: list[str] = []
    current = ""
    for raw_word in text.split():
        word = raw_word
        # A word that cannot fit on any line is hard-split across lines.
        while len(word) > width:
            if current:
                lines.append(current)
                current = ""
            lines.append(word[:width])
            word = word[width:]
        if not word:
            continue
        if not current:
            current = word
        elif len(current) + 1 + len(word) <= width:
            current = f"{current} {word}"
        else:
            lines.append(current)
            current = word

    if current:
        lines.append(current)
    return lines

files.src/textkit/truncate.py:
"""Length-limited text truncation."""

from __future__ import annotations

DEFAULT_SUFFIX = "..."


def truncate(text: str, limit: int, suffix: str = DEFAULT_SUFFIX) -> str:
    """Shorten ``text`` so it fits within ``limit`` characters.

    The returned string never exceeds ``limit``. When the text must be cut, the
    cut is made at a word boundary if one exists inside the available budget.

    Args:
        text: Input text.
        limit: Maximum length of the returned string, including ``suffix``.
        suffix: Marker appended when the text was shortened.

    Returns:
        The original text when it already fits, otherwise a shortened version
        no longer than ``limit``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``limit`` is negative.
    """
    if limit < 0:
        raise ValueError("limit must not be negative")
    if len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    if limit <= len(suffix):
        return suffix[:limit]

    budget = limit - len(suffix)
    head = text[:budget]
    boundary = head.rfind(" ")
    if boundary > 0:
        head = head[:boundary]
    return head.rstrip() + suffix

files.src/textkit/case.py:
"""Identifier case conversion."""

from __future__ import annotations


def snake_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Convert an identifier or phrase to ``snake_case``.

    Spaces, hyphens and underscores separate words. An uppercase letter starts
    a new word when it follows a lowercase letter or a digit, or when it follows
    another uppercase letter and is itself followed by a lowercase letter, so
    acronyms stay together (``HTTPServer`` -> ``http_server``).

    Args:
        text: Input identifier, e.g. ``camelCase``, ``PascalCase`` or
            ``kebab-case``.

    Returns:
        The ``snake_case`` form of ``text``.
    """
    pieces: list[str] = []
    for index, char in enumerate(text):
        if char in " -_":
            if pieces and pieces[-1] != "_":
                pieces.append("_")
            continue
        if char.isupper() and pieces and pieces[-1] != "_":
            previous = text[index - 1]
            following = text[index + 1] if index + 1 < len(text) else ""
            if (
                previous.islower()
                or previous.isdigit()
                or (previous.isupper() and following.islower())
            ):
                pieces.append("_")
        pieces.append(char.lower())
    return "".join(pieces).strip("_")

files.src/textkit/stats.py:
"""Simple text statistics."""

from __future__ import annotations


def word_count(text: str) -> int:
    """Return the number of words in ``text``.

    A word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters, where whitespace is
    anything ``str.isspace`` accepts (including Unicode spaces).

    Args:
        text: Input text.

    Returns:
        The number of words.
    """
    return len(text.split())

files.src/textkit/accents.py:
"""Diacritic removal."""

from __future__ import annotations

import unicodedata


def strip_accents(text: str) -> str:
    """Remove diacritical marks (accents) from ``text``.

    ``"café"`` becomes ``"cafe"``. Characters that carry no diacritic are
    returned unchanged.

    Args:
        text: Input text.

    Returns:
        ``text`` without diacritical marks.
    """
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", text)
    kept = "".join(char for char in decomposed if not unicodedata.combining(char))
    # Recompose so characters that NFD split without a diacritic (e.g. Hangul
    # syllables) come back as their original code points.
    return unicodedata.normalize("NFC", kept)

files.src/textkit/dedupe.py:
"""Order-preserving de-duplication."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterable


def dedupe_words(words: Iterable[str], *, case_sensitive: bool = True) -> list[str]:
    """Return ``words`` with duplicates removed, keeping first occurrences.

    The input is never modified and may be any iterable, including a one-shot
    iterator or generator.

    Args:
        words: The words to de-duplicate.
        case_sensitive: When False, words that differ only by case (compared
            with ``str.lower``) count as duplicates and the first spelling seen
            is kept.

    Returns:
        A new list of the de-duplicated words, in their original order.
    """
    seen: set[str] = set()
    result: list[str] = []
    for word in words:
        key = word if case_sensitive else word.lower()
        if key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            result.append(word)
    return result

files.src/textkit/pairs.py:
"""``key=value`` pair parsing."""

from __future__ import annotations


class ParseError(ValueError):
    """Raised when :func:`parse_pairs` cannot parse its input."""


def parse_pairs(text: str, sep: str = ";") -> dict[str, str]:
    """Parse ``"key=value; other=value"`` into a dictionary.

    Segments are separated by ``sep``; empty or whitespace-only segments are
    ignored. Keys and values are stripped of surrounding whitespace. When a key
    repeats, the last value wins. Only the first ``=`` separates the key from
    the value.

    Args:
        text: Input text.
        sep: Segment separator.

    Returns:
        The parsed pairs.

    Raises:
        ParseError: If a segment has no ``=`` or an empty key.
    """
    result: dict[str, str] = {}
    for segment in text.split(sep):
        stripped = segment.strip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        key, equals, value = stripped.partition("=")
        if not equals:
            raise ParseError(f"segment has no '=': {stripped!r}")
        if not key.strip():
            raise ParseError(f"segment has an empty key: {stripped!r}")
        result[key.strip()] = value.strip()
    return result

files.src/textkit/indent.py:
"""Line indentation."""

from __future__ import annotations


def indent(text: str, prefix: str, *, skip_blank: bool = False) -> str:
    """Add ``prefix`` to the start of every line of ``text``.

    Line endings (``\\n``, ``\\r\\n``) are preserved exactly, and no newline is
    added or removed.

    Args:
        text: Input text.
        prefix: String to put in front of each line.
        skip_blank: When True, lines that are empty or contain only whitespace
            are left unchanged instead of being prefixed.

    Returns:
        The indented text.
    """
    return "".join(
        line if skip_blank and not line.strip() else prefix + line
        for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    )

files.src/textkit/numbers.py:
"""Number formatting helpers."""

from __future__ import annotations


def format_count(count: int, noun: str, plural: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Format ``count`` together with a correctly pluralised ``noun``.

    Args:
        count: How many there are.
        noun: Singular form of the noun.
        plural: Plural form; defaults to ``noun + "s"``.

    Returns:
        For example ``"1 file"`` or ``"3 files"``.
    """
    word = noun if count == 1 else (plural if plural is not None else noun + "s")
    return f"{count} {word}"


def ordinal(n: int) -> str:
    """Return ``n`` with its English ordinal suffix, e.g. ``"21st"``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``n`` is not an ``int`` (``bool`` is rejected too).
        ValueError: If ``n`` is negative.
    """
    if isinstance(n, bool) or not isinstance(n, int):
        raise TypeError("ordinal() requires an int")
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("ordinal() requires a non-negative int")
    if n % 100 in (11, 12, 13):
        suffix = "th"
    else:
        suffix = {1: "st", 2: "nd", 3: "rd"}.get(n % 10, "th")
    return f"{n}{suffix}"

files.src/textkit/fields.py:
"""Delimited-field splitting."""

from __future__ import annotations


def split_fields(line: str, sep: str = ",") -> list[str]:
    """Split one delimited line into its fields.

    Fields are returned exactly as written: surrounding whitespace is kept, an
    empty input yields a single empty field, and a trailing separator yields a
    trailing empty field.

    A field that *starts* with a double quote is quoted: it extends to the
    matching closing quote, may contain ``sep``, and ``""`` inside it stands for
    one literal quote. The surrounding quotes are not part of the value. A
    quote anywhere else in a field is an ordinary character.

    Args:
        line: A single line of delimited text.
        sep: Field separator. Must be exactly one character.

    Returns:
        The fields, in order.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sep`` is not exactly one character, a quoted field is
            not terminated, or a closing quote is followed by anything other
            than ``sep`` or the end of the line.
    """
    if len(sep) != 1:
        raise ValueError("sep must be a single character")
    fields: list[str] = []
    pos, end = 0, len(line)
    while True:
        if pos < end and line[pos] == '"':
            chars: list[str] = []
            pos += 1
            while True:
                if pos >= end:
                    raise ValueError("unterminated quoted field")
                if line[pos] == '"':
                    if line[pos + 1 : pos + 2] == '"':
                        chars.append('"')
                        pos += 2
                        continue
                    pos += 1
                    break
                chars.append(line[pos])
                pos += 1
            if pos < end and line[pos] != sep:
                raise ValueError(f"unexpected character after closing quote at {pos}")
            fields.append("".join(chars))
        else:
            stop = line.find(sep, pos)
            stop = end if stop == -1 else stop
            fields.append(line[pos:stop])
            pos = stop
        if pos >= end:
            return fields
        pos += 1  # step over the separator

files.src/textkit/width.py:
"""Terminal display width and padding."""

from __future__ import annotations

import unicodedata

_ALIGNMENTS = ("left", "right", "center")


def _char_width(char: str) -> int:
    if unicodedata.combining(char) or unicodedata.category(char) == "Cf":
        return 0
    if unicodedata.east_asian_width(char) in ("W", "F"):
        return 2
    return 1


def display_width(text: str) -> int:
    """Return the number of terminal columns ``text`` occupies.

    Combining marks and zero-width format characters (category ``Cf``) take no
    columns, East Asian wide and fullwidth characters take two, and everything
    else takes one.

    Args:
        text: Input text.

    Returns:
        The display width in columns.
    """
    return sum(_char_width(char) for char in text)


def pad(text: str, width: int, align: str = "left") -> str:
    """Pad ``text`` with spaces so it occupies ``width`` display columns.

    Text that already occupies ``width`` columns or more is returned unchanged.
    When centring needs an odd number of spaces, the extra one goes on the right.

    Args:
        text: Input text.
        width: Target display width in columns.
        align: ``"left"``, ``"right"`` or ``"center"``.

    Returns:
        The padded text.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``align`` is not one of the supported values.
    """
    if align not in _ALIGNMENTS:
        raise ValueError(f"align must be one of {_ALIGNMENTS}")
    gap = width - display_width(text)
    if gap <= 0:
        return text
    if align == "right":
        return " " * gap + text
    if align == "center":
        left = gap // 2
        return " " * left + text + " " * (gap - left)
    return text + " " * gap

files.src/textkit/lines.py:
"""Line-oriented helpers."""

from __future__ import annotations


def line_range(text: str, first: int, last: int) -> list[str]:
    """Return lines ``first`` through ``last`` of ``text``, inclusive.

    Lines are numbered from 1, as in an editor. A ``last`` beyond the end of
    the text is clamped to the final line. Line endings are not included.

    Args:
        text: Input text.
        first: Number of the first line to return (1-based).
        last: Number of the last line to return (1-based, inclusive).

    Returns:
        The selected lines.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``first`` is less than 1 or ``last`` is less than
            ``first``.
    """
    if first < 1:
        raise ValueError("first must be at least 1")
    if last < first:
        raise ValueError("last must not be less than first")
    lines = text.splitlines()
    return lines[first - 1 : last]

files.src/textkit/chunks.py:
"""Fixed-size chunking."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
from itertools import islice
from typing import TypeVar

T = TypeVar("T")


def chunked(items: Iterable[T], size: int) -> Iterator[list[T]]:
    """Split ``items`` into consecutive chunks of ``size`` elements.

    Each chunk is a list. The last chunk may be shorter than ``size``. ``items``
    may be any iterable, including an infinite one: chunks are produced lazily
    and the source is consumed only as far as the chunks requested so far.

    Args:
        items: The elements to split.
        size: Chunk length. Must be at least 1.

    Returns:
        An iterator over the chunks, in order.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``size`` is less than 1 (raised at call time).
    """
    if size < 1:
        raise ValueError("size must be at least 1")
    source = iter(items)

    def generate() -> Iterator[list[T]]:
        while chunk := list(islice(source, size)):
            yield chunk

    return generate()
